clue.text: All that is required to run a shop?

definitions.text: All that is required to run a shop?

parts.words: All that is required to run a shop?
parts.note: read literally, the goods and equipment a shopkeeper needs; the phrase also means anyone's basic stock of skills or resources

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a plain question about retail; the answer is the idiom for the essential resources of any trade, here taken back to its literal shop sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the basic equipment, goods or skills a person or business relies on, which is exactly what a shop needs to operate.

clue.text: Essential tool for constructing a bridge?

definitions.text: Essential tool for constructing a bridge?

parts.words: Essential tool for constructing a bridge?
parts.note: a workshop tool for tightening nuts, and also literally something that spans a gap, as a bridge does

explanation.walkthrough: Builders of bridges do use this tool, but the pun is that the word also means 'one that spans', which is what a bridge itself does.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench-like tool turns nuts and bolts, and read as 'one who spans' the word describes a bridge's whole purpose.

clue.text: Do too much stuffing, maybe

parts.note: sounds like a cook packing a turkey, but means stuffing oneself with food past the point of need

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing' suggests the kitchen job of filling a bird; the person being stuffed is the eater.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge or eat to excess is to stuff oneself with more food than is needed.

clue.text: Irish university athlete among the exhibits at Cruft's?

parts.note: Kerry is a county in south-west Ireland, so it stands for something Irish
a Blue is a sportsman or sportswoman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University

explanation.surface: An Irish college sportsman turns up among the dogs on show at a famous show.
explanation.walkthrough: Cruft's is Britain's best-known dog show, so its exhibits are dogs; this is an Irish terrier breed with a blue-grey coat.
explanation.definitionFit: This Irish terrier breed is a pedigree dog of the kind shown at the big annual dog show.

clue.text: OT character who foresaw human error

indicators.note: the word human is set down in error, its letters in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An Old Testament seer predicted that people would go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' turns HUMAN into the name of a minor prophet; OT is the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of the twelve minor prophets of the Old Testament, whose book foretells the fall of Nineveh.

clue.text: The way in which a dangerous mission is accomplished?

definitions.text: The way in which a dangerous mission is accomplished?

parts.words: The way in which a dangerous mission is accomplished?
parts.note: the manner of carrying out a hazardous task, taken as an adverb describing how it is done

explanation.walkthrough: The question asks for a manner, so the answer is an adverb meaning with danger to oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning in a hazardous or perilous way, the manner of any dangerous undertaking.

clue.text: Free to operate a door-to-door service?

definitions.meaning: to release or rescue, as in being saved from evil
to take letters or goods round to people's houses

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go freelance and run a doorstep round.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free or rescue someone, and also to bring post or goods round to each home, as a postman or milkman does.

clue.text: Stock-cars that need powerful engines to pull them along

definitions.text: Stock-cars that need powerful engines to pull them along

parts.words: Stock-cars that need powerful engines to pull them along
parts.note: stock-cars suggest motor racing, but here stock means livestock and the cars are railway wagons hauled by a locomotive

explanation.walkthrough: Stock-car racing comes to mind first; the engines are railway locomotives and the stock is farm animals carried in wagons.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway wagons for carrying livestock are pulled by a locomotive, and stock is another word for farm animals.

clue.text: He gets nothing but pleasure from playing the game .

definitions.text: He gets nothing but pleasure from playing the game

parts.words: He gets nothing but pleasure from playing the game
parts.note: sounds like a happy player, but means one who is paid nothing and plays only for love of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing but pleasure' reads as pure joy; it means he earns no money, only enjoyment, since the word comes from the Latin for lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional sportsman plays without pay, for enjoyment alone.

clue.text: … and hurtles all over the place, this energetic fellow

indicators.note: the letters of hurtles are scattered everywhere and must be regrouped

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a lively man rushes about in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' signals an anagram of HURTLES; the leading dots link the clue to the one before.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-getter who works with drive and push, pressing hard for business or success.

clue.text: Reason why a RU scrum is difficult to bring under control!

definitions.note: an adjective phrase describing the answer, a bolting animal hard to stop

indicators.note: a rugby scrum is a jumbled heap of players, so these letters are piled up in a new order

explanation.surface: A rugby union scrum is hard to keep in check, and this explains why.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is Rugby Union; 'scrum' rearranges REASON WHY A RU. The definition describes the answer rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolting steed that has thrown off the rider's command is by nature very hard to rein in.

clue.text: Essay about the last Stuart leather manufactory

indicators.note: the word for an attempt goes around the name of the queen

parts.note: to essay something is to try it
Queen Anne was the last monarch of the House of Stuart

explanation.surface: An academic essay on Queen Anne somehow lands in a leather works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essay' looks like a piece of writing but is the verb meaning attempt; 'about' is the container signal, and the Stuart dynasty ended with Queen Anne in 1714.
explanation.definitionFit: A works where hides are cured and turned into leather.

clue.text: Armoured vehicle used for carrying messages?

definitions.text: Armoured vehicle used for carrying messages?

parts.words: Armoured vehicle used for carrying messages?
parts.note: chain armour is called mail, and letters are also mail, so the van is armoured only in a punning sense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Armoured vehicle' suggests a military tank; the armour is mail, which is also the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A Post Office van carries letters and parcels, and mail doubles as the word for chain armour.

clue.text: A wading-bird the Engineers get excited about

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up and moved about into a new order

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers grow animated over a bird in the shallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited about' shuffles RE plus GET.
explanation.definitionFit: A white heron that wades in shallow water to catch fish.

clue.text: Sweep in which one wins a horseshoe magnet, for instance?

definitions.text: Sweep in which one wins a horseshoe magnet, for instance?

parts.words: Sweep in which one wins a horseshoe magnet, for instance?
parts.note: a horseshoe is a token of good fortune and a magnet attracts, so the prize itself is fortunate and pulls

explanation.walkthrough: A sweep is a sweepstake; a horseshoe is fortunate and a magnet draws things to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle or sweepstake in which prizes go to tickets picked at random.

clue.text: An application that can make a lady go momentarily white

definitions.text: An application that can make a lady go momentarily white

parts.words: An application that can make a lady go momentarily white
parts.note: a face ointment smeared on looks white, as if the wearer had turned pale with fright

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go white' suggests fear; the whiteness is a cosmetic smeared on the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick cleansing ointment for the skin, white when spread on the face.

clue.text: A revolver not designed for use at the front

definitions.text: A revolver not designed for use at the front

parts.words: A revolver not designed for use at the front
parts.note: a revolver suggests a pistol carried at the battle front; here it is anything that turns, fitted at the back of a vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' and 'the front' suggest a gun in the trenches; the thing revolving is on the back axle of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the back pair of tyred discs on a car, turning on the rear axle.

clue.text: Kind of Laotian tree noted for its lofty beauty

definitions.text: tree noted for its lofty beauty

indicators.note: suggests a version of the word Laotian, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree from Laos is admired for its height and looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' rearranges LAOTIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree of heaven, a tall ornamental tree whose name comes from a word meaning tree of the skies.

clue.text: Angry gathering that makes us a little depressed?

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in not a whit
feeling low means feeling down

explanation.surface: A furious crowd leaves everyone feeling a bit downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'gathering' is also a gathering of pus, and 'angry' describes inflamed skin, so this is not a crowd but a sore on a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed abscess at the fingertip, a red pus-filled swelling.

clue.text: My first insert is far from clear

indicators.note: the abbreviation for first is put inside the word My

parts.note: taken as written
1st, written with a numeral one that reads as the letter I

explanation.surface: A writer frets that their first insertion is murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insert' is the container signal; the old crossword trick writes 'first' as 1ST and reads the numeral one as a capital I.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazy or foggy, so blurred and hard to see.

clue.text: A pupil given special authority to drive round Northern Ireland

indicators.note: the word for driving goes round the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

parts.note: to motor is to travel by car

explanation.surface: A trusted schoolchild is allowed to drive around Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal; 'to drive' must be read as a verb, as in to travel by car, and the pupil is a school prefect-style post.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior schoolchild trusted with duties such as keeping order in class.

clue.text: Creatures that thrive in the main

definitions.text: Creatures that thrive in the main

parts.words: Creatures that thrive in the main
parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the ocean, though it reads as 'mostly'

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'on the whole'; the main is the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine fish living in salt water rather than rivers or lakes.

clue.text: Operator of a big fiddle serving a prison sentence?

definitions.text: Operator of a big fiddle serving a prison sentence?

parts.words: Operator of a big fiddle serving a prison sentence?
parts.note: a big fiddle suggests a swindle and so jail; it is a large stringed instrument

explanation.walkthrough: A 'fiddle' is a fraud, which leads to a cell; the big fiddle is the instrument larger than a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays the large bowed instrument held between the knees.

clue.text: Express mild disapprobation over gold coach

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the second

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone tuts at a gilded stagecoach.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' places TUT above OR.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to give private teaching, as a private teacher does.

clue.text: Can vote anew to get some money abroad

indicators.note: the letters of can vote are made again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Voters go back to the polls to get funds overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anew' rearranges CAN VOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small coin worth one hundredth of a peso or similar unit in several Latin American countries.

clue.text: Type of undergarment an athlete may wear out

definitions.text: Type of undergarment an athlete may wear out

parts.words: Type of undergarment an athlete may wear out
parts.note: a vest normally worn under clothes, but a runner wears it outside as the top garment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wear out' suggests wearing it to rags; it means wearing it on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless vest worn under a shirt or as a sports top.

clue.text: Necessitates a silent modification

indicators.note: the letters of a silent are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A quiet change is called for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modification' rearranges A SILENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To involve or require something as a consequence.

clue.text: An advance order

parts.note: reads as an order placed beforehand, but is a military command to advance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance order' sounds like booking ahead; it is the parade-ground command to step off.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill command telling troops to start moving ahead.
